project.name: Barbershop Booking Website Template
project.goal: Build a customizable barbershop website with booking system, multi-language support, admin and employee dashboards, email confirmations, gallery, and offers page. Each client will get an independent deployment with custom branding and content.

roles.name: shop_admin
roles.description: Manages the entire barbershop website, employees, services, bookings, offers, gallery, and settings.

roles.name: employee
roles.description: Can view assigned bookings, manage availability if allowed, and update booking statuses.

roles.name: customer
roles.description: Public visitor who can browse the website and book an appointment without registration.

business_rules: Customers can book without creating an account.
A booking is directly created with status 'confirmed'.
Customers can choose a specific employee or select any available employee.
Each employee has different working hours.
Service duration and price are not fixed globally; they depend on the employee.
Only employees assigned to a service can be booked for that service.
Available time slots must be generated based on employee working hours, existing bookings, blocked times, and service duration for that employee.
The system must prevent overlapping bookings.
The system must send a confirmation email after a successful booking.
Each shop will have an independent deployment, but the codebase should be reusable as a template.

data_model_notes.important_rule: Service duration and price must be stored in the employee-service relation, not only in the service itself.

development_phases.name: Project setup and architecture
includes: Initialize Next.js project with TypeScript and Tailwind CSS
Set up Prisma and MySQL/MariaDB connection
Configure Auth.js for admin and employee authentication

development_phases.name: Database schema and core models
includes: Seed initial admin user and demo content

development_phases.name: Booking system
includes: Implement employee selection including any available employee

development_phases.name: Email and polish
includes: Improve UX, validation, and responsive design
Test role-based access and booking edge cases

non_functional_requirements: Use clean and modular folder structure
Use server-side validation for booking and admin actions
Protect admin and employee routes with role-based authorization
Prevent race conditions or duplicate bookings for the same time slot
Ensure responsive layout across mobile and desktop
Keep the code reusable for future client deployments

implementation_style: Use clean architecture and modular components
Prefer server actions or route handlers where appropriate
Make forms validated with Zod if possible
Make the project production-ready, not just a demo
